title: Dairy-Free Peach & Vanilla Cupcakes
shortDescription: Soft vanilla cupcakes with real peach puree frosting, ready in 25 minutes prep and 18 minutes bake.
description: These cupcakes came from a summer with too many ripe peaches on my counter. I cooked some down into a thick puree and swirled it into dairy-free frosting instead of jam on the side. The cake base is plain vanilla, made with almond milk and neutral oil so it stays moist without butter. It is a good template if you bake for a friend who cannot have dairy but still wants a classic bakery cupcake. The frosting is the fun part. Cooked peach puree gets folded into dairy-free butter and powdered sugar, so you get real fruit flavor and a soft peach color with no food dye. I tested this three times in my kitchen before the puree ratio was right. Too much puree made the frosting slide off, so cook it down well and let it cool completely first.
ingredients: 1 1/2 cups fresh peaches, peeled and diced (about 2 medium peaches)
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Line a 12-cup muffin pan with paper liners.
In a small saucepan, cook diced peaches with lemon juice over medium heat for 8 minutes, until soft and thick. Cool completely.
In a bowl, whisk flour, baking powder, and salt together.
In another bowl, beat oil and sugar until combined. Add eggs one at a time, then vanilla.
Add flour mix and almond milk in three batches, alternating, starting and ending with flour. Mix just until smooth.
Divide batter evenly among liners, filling each about two thirds full.
Bake 18 to 20 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool in the pan 5 minutes, then move to a rack.
For frosting, beat dairy-free butter until fluffy, about 2 minutes. Add powdered sugar in two batches, beating well.
Fold in 1/3 cup cooled peach puree until the frosting is smooth and lightly peach colored. Chill 10 minutes if too soft to pipe.
Pipe frosting onto cooled cupcakes and top with a small spoon of leftover peach puree.
tips: Cook the peach puree until thick like jam, not runny, or the frosting will not hold its shape.
Let both the cupcakes and puree cool fully before frosting, warm cake melts dairy-free butter fast.
No fresh peaches? Use 1 1/2 cups canned peaches, drained well, and cook the same way.
Chill piped cupcakes for 15 minutes before serving in warm weather, dairy-free frosting softens quickly.

faq.question: Can I use frozen peaches for this recipe?
faq.answer: Yes. Thaw and drain frozen peaches first, then cook them the same way as fresh. They release more water, so simmer a few extra minutes to thicken the puree.

faq.question: Why is my peach frosting runny?
faq.answer: The puree likely was not cooked down enough or was added warm. Cook it until thick and jam-like, then cool it fully before folding it into the frosting.

faq.question: Is this recipe egg-free too?
faq.answer: Not as written, it uses two eggs in the cake. You can try a flax egg swap, but I have not tested that version in my own kitchen yet.

faq.question: How long do these cupcakes stay fresh?
faq.answer: Store them in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days. Bring to room temperature for about 20 minutes before serving for the best texture.

conclusion: This is my go-to cupcake when peaches are in season and someone at the table cannot have dairy. The puree frosting tastes like real fruit, not artificial peach flavor, and it never lasts long on my counter.
